question: Should `promptly-prompt` be accepted as an OpenClaw code plugin after it gains a valid OpenClaw package entrypoint, or should this repository remain publishable only as a skill/Claude plugin?
rationale: The artifact advertises OpenClaw compatibility but its current executable behavior is Claude-specific and does not satisfy ClawHub's code-plugin package contract, so the permanent package family cannot be inferred safely from metadata alone.

options.title: Require a valid OpenClaw plugin
options.body: Keep this issue open until the publisher supplies the required package manifest and OpenClaw entrypoint, passes validation and scans, and demonstrates a real install and prompt-hook run.

options.title: Route to skill-only publishing
options.body: Ask the publisher to use the existing skill publishing path and decline a plugin catalog entry unless an OpenClaw-compatible runtime is added.

recommendation.title: Require a valid OpenClaw plugin
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the publisher supplies the required package manifest and OpenClaw entrypoint, passes validation and scans, and demonstrates a real install and prompt-hook run.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current plugin-family, validation, provenance, and publishing contract that governs this choice.
